subject: french
title: Stamp 3: Relative Clauses and Gerund
welcome_lead: Link your ideas with relative pronouns and the gerund.
meta_desc: A-Level French adventure on relative clauses (qui, que, dont), present participle and gerund, and indirect speech.
final_note: Stamp complete! Your sentences will now flow naturally.

concepts.def: Relative pronoun acting as the subject of the relative clause: l'homme qui parle.
Relative pronoun acting as the object of the relative clause: le livre que je lis.
Relative pronoun replacing de + noun: la femme dont je parle (the woman of whom I speak).
Form ending in -ant, used as adjective or to express simultaneous action: parlant, ayant, etant.
Formed with en + present participle, expressing manner or simultaneity: en marchant.
Reporting what someone said using que, with appropriate tense shifts: Il a dit qu'il viendrait.

walkthroughs.body_html: Use qui when the relative pronoun is the subject of the verb that follows: la fille qui chante (the girl who sings). Use que when it is the object: le film que j'ai vu (the film that I saw).
Le livre dont je parle est interessant — the book that I am speaking about is interesting. Dont replaces de + le livre. Also used for possession: la maison dont le toit est rouge.
Il est parti en courant — he left running. En lisant, on apprend — by reading, one learns. The gerund describes how or when something happens.
